selectedFiles.reason: Actual runtime producer: assistant mode, current intentional full-access profile for every agent, spawn-bound paths/approval IDs, trusted job owner and serialized client dispatch. Compare the real producer with template declarations and the SDK comment; do not infer that a declared template profile is enforced.

Current production-contract tests explicitly expect full-access even when a template declares git-commit or librarian-read-only; approval receipt forwarding is independently asserted. This establishes the deliberate policy choice and prevents treating old clamping comments as current wiring.

Real terminal consumer: resolves cwd, overwrites owner with trusted state, threads env and AbortSignal, classifies approvals, consumes/grants repository/workspace/root-run/snapshot/command-hash-bound receipts, and exposes denial versus unavailable approval context. Its profile-clamping comment differs from the current runtime producer above.

Complete SYNC/BACKGROUND execution function: cwd containment, optional lexical profiles, exact-action/hash approval rerun preserving mode/profile, staged-commit preflight, merged credential scrubbing, direct bash spawning, detach/abort races, output spool, timeout/TERM/KILL, exit/error results and dirty-path observation. Verify current default full-access runtime separately from the SDK helper's workspace-write default.

Public policy evaluator and every permission-profile branch, user/full-access exemptions, quote-aware helper calls, traversal/absolute path checks, command/environment deny lists and parse-fallback behavior. Helpers are secondary slices; this is lexical policy, not OS enforcement or a shipped Rust shell parser.

Raw host environment export versus copied canonical credential denylist scrub, caller override re-scrub and platform case handling. Compare actual callers below with the helper rather than inferring all spawned processes use it.

Actual detached shell process launch, safe job log creation, owner/registry registration, chunk/line output, quota kill and child exit/error settlement. Check supplied environment and descendant cleanup against the shared termination helper in secondary files.

Recovered-process identity probe, Linux start-time fencing, live/recovered TERM/KILL paths, stopping versus stopped state, bounded escalation and refusal to kill unverifiable/recycled pids. Recovery data integrity and mutation rollback remain outside pair09.

Real validation/hook effect path: configured/inferred hooks, no-hooks/skipped states, Promise.allSettled concurrency, default runTerminalCommand call without the terminal dispatcher approval callback or runtime profile, per-file command quoting, output diagnostics and abort rethrow. Separate this from the diagnostic-delta argv path below.

Production compiler/diagnostic argv launcher and hook injector: direct injected spawn, inherited/merged host env, timeout TERM/KILL, byte-bounded capture, native AbortSignal handoff and fail-open injection/baseline policy. Trace run.ts creation and consumers through secondary ranges.

Actual TypeScript LSP process adapter/factory: on-demand multiplexer creation, direct argv spawn with cwd-only options, child kill adapter and filesystem document-open bridge. Inspect environment, effect policy and run cancellation at this producer; semantic mutations belong to pair06 and language query semantics to pair07.

Complete generic TypeScript sidecar supervisor class: subprocess env overrides, handshake/request framing, pending/time/output bounds, stderr error tail, stop/start/restart races, give-up and TERM/KILL cleanup. Compare its request protocol with the Rust exec role and search for an actual production constructor consumer.

Actual browser process effects: pipe/port launch options, inherited environment, Chrome sandbox arguments, private temporary user-data dirs, protocol capability fallback, startup/exit registration and stop-during-spawn rollback. Runtime ownership and teardown/sandbox probes are secondary; browser interaction quality is pair13.

Actual MCP launch/connect boundary: shared cache/single-flight construction, stdio subprocess env and ignored stderr, remote transport/DNS pinning, connect completion and client registration. Pair10 owns origins, descriptors and plugin trust; pair09 checks process/env/deadline/cancel/egress enforcement and adoption only.

Real native exec role protocol: version handshake, line-delimited stdin parsing, malformed/EOF failures, ExecPlan deserialize and runner delegation, plus pure handshake tests. Compare with the generic supervisor's correlated request protocol; inspect boundedness and honest TS consumer availability.

Real OS execution: apply Landlock first on Linux, emit enforcement/degraded status, optional env_clear, Unix exec replacement and non-Unix spawn/wait/exit. Current scope excludes brush-parser, bwrap, seccomp, Seatbelt and Windows restricted-token enforcement unless adjacent current code proves them.

Actual Linux kernel ruleset and its test: ABI V1, path FD allow-read/allow-write, fully/partially/not-enforced classification, missing path/syscall errors and thread-scoped test isolation. Compare current guarantee with the latest D48 amendment, not obsolete D4.

Shipped workspace/role/PTY charter and build/testing/package claims. Check its all-role not_implemented wording against current Exec dispatch and CI/archive consumers; docs are a claim boundary, not evidence that PTY/jobd/native adoption is shipped.
